elements.element: This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of New York.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 expressly provides that the Agreement is governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York.

elements.element: The state and federal courts located in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 grants those courts exclusive jurisdiction generally, but permits either Party to seek temporary injunctive relief in another court for confidential-information or intellectual-property protection. The required exclusive jurisdiction is therefore qualified.

elements.element: This Agreement is governed by the laws of Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Section 28.1 selects New York law, not any permitted fallback law.

elements.element: The selected courts are the corresponding courts of Delaware or California, or the courts of London where England and Wales law applies.
elements.evidence: Section 28.2 selects courts located in New York County rather than courts in Delaware, California, or London.

result.reason: The redline selects the preferred New York governing law and generally selects the preferred New York County courts. However, the express right to seek temporary injunctive relief in another court prevents the forum provision from providing unqualified exclusive jurisdiction as required by the preferred position. No fallback is satisfied because neither fallback law nor fallback courts are selected. The redline preserves unrelated terms and does not introduce an internal contradiction, but it does not make all changes necessary to achieve a complete preferred or fallback position.
